title: Incident Record
description: One real world event, written once and cited by every scenario that draws on it. An incident is the evidence a scenario stands on: the scenario says what an attacker did and what we would see, the incident says it actually happened, to whom, and who said so. Disagreement between sources is recorded in `contested`, never resolved by the analyst. Files live in incidents/<slug>.yaml and the validator enforces that every slug a scenario cites exists here.

slug.description: Stable kebab-case handle. Must equal the filename without .yaml. Immutable once a scenario cites it.

title.description: What happened, as a headline a non-specialist can read.

date.description: When it happened, YYYY-MM-DD. A range is written YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD when the event spanned days. Quote it in YAML so it stays a string.

disclosed.description: When it became public, YYYY-MM-DD, when that differs from date. The gap between the two is itself a fact worth keeping.

what_happened.description: The event in plain terms. What was reached, by what route, and what the consequence was. No speculation; unresolved claims go in contested.

source.description: Attribution line: who disclosed or researched it, and when. The citations themselves are in references.

scenarios.description: Scenario ids this incident grounds. The validator checks each exists and warns when a scenario cites this incident without appearing here, so the join reads the same from both sides.

references.description: Tiered citations. Same shape as scenario provenance.sources and use case sources, deliberately, so a citation reads identically on every record type.

tier.description: 0 first party: the affected party's own disclosure or the researcher's own writeup. 1 reputable secondary technical reporting. 2 press, aggregators and summaries. Quoted strings.

note.description: What this source contributes, or what it gets wrong. Disagreement between sources is recorded here and in contested, not resolved.

contested.description: Claims the parties disagree about. Each holds every position verbatim with its attribution. The analyst records the disagreement and its status; the analyst does not pick a winner.

positions.description: One entry per party, prefixed with the party in square brackets, quoting their words.

notes.description: Analyst working notes. Why the incident is in the library, what secondary reporting gets wrong, what to verify before citing externally. Never rendered.
